page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.metal-24xl is a general-purpose bare-metal server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities, achieving high-ranking results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core workloads. Memory performance is highly efficient, with DDR5 memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores ranking in the top tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top tier, supported by the high-speed local NVMe storage. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category.

The server offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads due to its 96 dedicated physical cores and integrated high-capacity NVMe storage. The lack of simultaneous multithreading means each core runs a single dedicated thread, which ensures predictable execution but limits thread-level parallelism compared to hyperthreaded architectures. Additionally, while the system handles medium and large LLM text generation with strong relative performance, small model text generation benchmarks are notably weak.

The m8gd.metal-24xl is suited for high-throughput database deployments, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and software compilation pipelines. Its balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio and large local NVMe storage also make it appropriate for multi-threaded data processing, containerized microservices, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring bare-metal performance without virtualization overhead.
